concerns.text: The plan proposes implementing Repeated Measures ANOVA (RM-ANOVA) manually using `numpy` and `scipy.stats` because `scipy` lacks a native function. This introduces high risk of implementation error in the error term calculation (Subject vs. Residual). A manual implementation of RM-ANOVA is not a standard, validated statistical method and threatens the validity of the F-statistic and p-values required for the causal claim.

The plan states: 'Use `scipy.stats.f_oneway` on the difference scores'. This is methodologically incorrect for a 2-condition within-subjects design. `f_oneway` performs a One-Way ANOVA on independent groups. Applying it to difference scores (which are single values per subject) is mathematically equivalent to a one-sample t-test against zero, not an ANOVA. This misapplication of the test statistic invalidates the planned analysis for FR-002.

The plan mandates Shapiro-Wilk on 'difference scores' but states 'ANOVA is mandated' regardless of normality. While robust, RM-ANOVA is sensitive to violations of normality in small samples (N=30). The plan lacks a contingency for non-normal data (e.g., Wilcoxon Signed-Rank test) which is the standard non-parametric equivalent for this design. Relying solely on ANOVA when assumptions fail risks Type I/II errors.

The plan targets N=30 participants. For a within-subjects design with 3 metrics (Time, Errors, SUS) and a medium effect size (f=0.25), N=30 yields power ~0.65-0.70, not the standard 0.80. The plan acknowledges this in `power_analyzer.py` but does not adjust the recruitment target or the statistical power threshold, risking an underpowered study that cannot support the intended conclusions.
